claim: Rugix Ctrl v1.4.0 is the latest release (published 2026-11-02); the tag points to commit 6d7fc277919b0048893c80d7e1e6e488ddc7b27b

Rugix Bakery v0.9.4 (published 2026-08-20) is the latest Bakery release; its container image ghcr.io/rugix/rugix-bakery:v0.9.4 has digest sha256:abd9f86531f004d76ba73783e4e2d4f8046857c28a8786a435f67d45fc87a58b (arm64 pull)

In Rugix's GRUB boot flow the first-stage script resets rugpi_boot_spare to false and saves it before booting the spare partition, so a trial boot is one-shot and any later reboot without commit returns to the default partition
Rugix Ctrl's default boot flows (uboot, grub, systemd-boot) have no dead man's switch and Rugix Ctrl does not mark boot groups good or bad automatically; an external mechanism must do it

Rugix docs warn the Bakery auto-commit recipe commits whatever system it boots into, including an old version booted during a rollback, and recommend a pre-commit hook so only a healthy system can be committed
In Bakery v0.9.4 the auto-commit recipe directory is named rugpi-auto-commit (docs call it core/rugix-auto-commit) and its unit runs 'rugix-ctrl system commit' unconditionally

Rugix Ctrl changes the boot flow only after all payloads have completed and their state is saved; power loss before that boundary can leave data in an inactive slot but Rugix does not select it for boot
Rugix Ctrl's default bootstrapping layout uses a 4 GiB system slot size
Bakery's default generic-grub-efi image layout is GPT: 256 MiB FAT32 config, 256 MiB ext4 boot-a, 256 MiB boot-b, then system-a (ext4 without journal unless squashfs)

Rugix's own interruption test performs a soft 'reboot -f' after 64 MiB written to the target slot and asserts the device boots the active slot (default=a, active=a); it does not simulate a hard power cut
Rugix Bakery requires a privileged container (chroot and bind mounts)
With Rugix state management the root overlay is discarded on every boot by default; only declared persist paths survive
Rugix Ctrl 1.0.0 made bundle signatures mandatory unless opted out
k3s v1.37.2+k3s1 was published 2026-11-03 and the k3s stable channel redirected to it on 2026-11-10
Debian stable is 13.7 'trixie' (Release file dated 2026-09-12)
Bakery's debian-bootstrap recipe can pin all packages to a snapshot.debian.org timestamp via its snapshot parameter
umbrelOS commits the running Rugix slot as soon as umbreld starts ('If we've successfully booted then commit to the current OS partition'); no app or service health check precedes the commit
umbrelOS installs updates with 'rugix-ctrl update install --reboot set' and reads the boot flow from 'rugix-ctrl system info --json' (camelCase key bootFlow)
umbrelOS's amd64 Bakery layer pins Rugix Ctrl v1.3.2 (glibc build), one minor version behind the latest 1.4.0
Lab: Rugix Bakery v0.9.4 built bootable Debian 13 generic-grub-efi images and update bundles for arm64 (native, ~5 min) and amd64 (binfmt emulation in an arm64 Lima VM, ~12 min) on an Apple M5 Max
Lab: first-boot bootstrapping of the Bakery image on a 24 GB disk created system-b and data partitions with 4 GiB system slots and a 15.2 GiB ext4 data partition

Lab: on arm64 (run 4) a good update committed via the k3s health gate, a bad update (k3s fails to start) rolled back automatically after the 300 s gate deadline, a manual commit on the bad slot was refused by the pre-commit hook, and a QEMU SIGKILL at 440 MiB written left the old slot booting with a clean reinstall afterwards

Lab: because k3s state persists across A/B slot switches, a health check that only reads node Ready and CoreDNS availableReplicas from the API passed within 0-20 s and committed an update whose kubelet never runs (--disable-agent), on both arm64 and amd64; a check adding local kubelet /healthz, node heartbeat newer than boot and CoreDNS Ready-since-boot rolled the same update back

Lab: a gate that rolls back on the first refused commit reverted a good update under slow x86 emulation because CoreDNS status flapped (stale available, then recreated); requiring 3 consecutive fresh checks and retrying until the deadline fixed it in run 4
Lab: in the QEMU guest the k3s kubelet healthz listened only on [::1]:10248 (node IP was IPv6), so a probe of 127.0.0.1:10248 fails

Lab: in a Bakery child layer, declaring a dependency on a recipe already applied in the parent re-ran that recipe after the dependent one, resetting its files (recipe order [3/5] break-k3s then [4/5] install k3s)
Lab: 'rugix-ctrl system info' (1.4.0) prints JSON with camelCase keys (boot.activeGroup, boot.defaultGroup)
